points.description: States what the table holds: a mapping of destination stations/MAC addresses to the outgoing LAN interface/port (which LAN each station can be reached over).
points.partial_credit: Half if only says it holds addresses or ports without the mapping between them.

points.description: Describes how the table is modified in backward learning: starts empty; on receiving a frame with source address Q on LAN L, the bridge adds/updates the entry 'Q reachable via L' (timestamped, old entries purged), i.e. learns from observed incoming traffic.
points.partial_credit: Half if it says the table is filled from incoming traffic but omits the use of the source address and arrival LAN.

points.description: Describes use in forwarding: the bridge looks up the frame's destination address and forwards it only on the associated link (flooding if unknown).
points.partial_credit: Half if it says the table is looked up for forwarding without destination-to-link detail.

points.description: Gives one benefit: selective forwarding instead of flooding, reducing unnecessary traffic/duplication/congestion or improving bandwidth use.
points.partial_credit: Half if benefit is vague (e.g. 'more efficient') without reference to reduced flooding or traffic.

rubric.notes: Each of the four parts asked for (table contents, learning update, use in forwarding, one benefit) is worth a quarter mark. Accept different wording, but the mapping of MAC/station to LAN/port and learning from the source address of incoming frames must be present. Vague or half-stated parts earn half of that quarter; a wrong statement loses only that part.
